attribution.note: Marcus states and endorses the claim in his own argument.

semantics.note: The normalization preserves the claim about encoding and guaranteeing broad constraints. In context, it describes the technical position when Sora was announced.

contract.note: The contextual reading of Sora and comparable general-purpose systems is ordinary and fair. Distinguishing broad guarantees from isolated mathematical constraints, and missing guarantees from unavailable enforcement methods, materially determines the assessment.

evidence.note: OpenAI's contemporaneous disclosure documents physical and continuity failures. It establishes implementation failures, not the absence of an applicable enforcement method.
The pre-post theoretical result concerns learning computable ground-truth functions. Its formal scope does not establish the claimed lack of enforcement methods across Sora and comparable systems.
The specialized GAN enforces mass conservation, demonstrating a narrow constraint mechanism. It does not guarantee the named broad properties in a comparable general-purpose system.
The result depends on calibration and particular fact types. Possible mitigation of other errors neither supplies a broad guarantee nor establishes that such guarantees were unavailable.

reviews.rationale: The packet documents Sora's failures and limited theoretical barriers, but does not establish that broad constraint enforcement was technically unavailable in February 2024. The specialized hard-constraint method supplies no qualifying counterexample. Neither resolution condition is met.
